hero.tagline: Where we lead, where we lag, and what to build next.
hero.subtitle: A grounded analysis of nuPilot Campaign Studio against the two enterprise AI marketing platforms our buyers benchmark against in 2026.

tldr.sub: What's actually true once you read the matrix in Section 04.
paragraphs: Campaign Studio is not sitting in the middle of Jasper and Skai. It looks like Jasper on the surface (content, workflows, brand, approvals) and runs like Skai underneath, with scale, reliability, and governance baked in. But it doesn't yet own the features customers actually buy from either platform.

It owns the foundation they sit on. Reproducibility, live tracking, approval gates, encrypted credentials, tenant isolation. These are the bones; the muscle on top is the work for the next two quarters.

capabilities.name: Brand voice & guidelines
capabilities.reality: We can store voice, look, and pillars. We can't yet enforce them at generation time.

capabilities.name: One-click brand from a URL
capabilities.reality: Jasper scrapes a company website and builds the brand profile. We start blank.

capabilities.name: AI search readiness score
capabilities.reality: Jasper grades content for AI search before publish. We don't score yet.

capabilities.name: Bulk content packs
capabilities.reality: One brief to many assets. Jasper ships templates; we run it manually.

capabilities.name: Content generation at scale
capabilities.reality: Both Jasper and we generate at volume; Skai is not a content tool.

capabilities.name: Bid optimization
capabilities.reality: Skai has 15 years of ML bidding. Neither Jasper nor we play here.

capabilities.name: Budget pacing
capabilities.reality: Skai paces spend across networks live. We can cap, not pace.

capabilities.name: Retail network breadth
capabilities.reality: Skai integrates 100+ networks. We integrate the few our buyers use.

capabilities.name: Attribution & measurement
capabilities.reality: Skai owns this; Jasper and we report at the campaign level only.

capabilities.name: Live run tracking
capabilities.reality: Watch every step as it happens, resumes cleanly across devices. Ours alone.

capabilities.name: Human approval gates
capabilities.reality: Approve, reject, or rewrite a step mid-run with a recorded decision.

capabilities.name: Reproducible campaigns
capabilities.reality: Re-run next month, get an identical result. Neither competitor guarantees this.

capabilities.name: Multi-tenant isolation
capabilities.reality: Data, spend, and limits walled off per customer from day one.

capabilities.name: Connector auto-recovery
capabilities.reality: Connectors detect outages, hold, probe, and resume with no operator.

ahead.sub: Engineering moats Jasper and Skai don't trivially copy. Defend these; they're the wedge for enterprise sales.

items.title: Reproducible campaigns
items.body: Re-run the same campaign next month and get an identical result. Neither Jasper nor Skai offers this guarantee.

items.title: Live run tracking
items.body: Watch every campaign step as it happens. Refresh, drop network, switch devices, the view resumes cleanly.

items.title: Human approval gates
items.body: A reviewer can approve, reject, or rewrite a step mid-campaign. The workflow pauses, the decision is recorded, execution resumes.

items.title: Connector reliability
items.body: When a vendor goes down or a credential expires, our connectors detect, hold, probe for recovery, and resume, with no operator intervention.

items.title: Enterprise-grade isolation
items.body: Every customer's data, spend, and limits walled off from day one. No retrofitting needed for compliance.

closeable.sub: Each gap maps to existing schema or services. Six items, all shippable inside thirteen weeks.

items.title: AI search readiness score
items.desc: A scorer that grades content against AI search guidelines before publish

items.title: One-click brand from URL
items.desc: Scrape a company website and auto-fill brand voice, audience, and knowledge base

items.title: Bulk content-pack template
items.desc: One brief in → blog post, social captions, newsletter, and ad script out, in one run

items.title: Campaign comparison dashboard
items.desc: Side-by-side view of cost, completion rate, and outcomes across campaigns

items.title: Finish AI tool refresh
items.desc: The last piece of plumbing to keep connected vendor tools auto-updated

items.title: UTM auto-tagging
items.desc: Stamp every campaign output with the right tracking parameters automatically

decisions.sub: Not engineering tasks. These get decided in a leadership room, not a sprint.

items.title: Bidding
items.body: Do we play in bid optimization at all? Skai has fifteen years of ML bidding behind their engine. We'd be three engineers deep before we caught up.

items.title: Retail networks
items.body: Match Skai's 100+ network coverage, or pick the three our buyers actually use? This is a partnerships problem, not a coding one.

items.title: SOC 2
items.body: When does SOC 2 stop being optional? Six months and roughly $60k once we start. The trigger is usually the first enterprise procurement call.

items.title: In-product chat
items.body: Do we build chat at all, or assume buyers will use ChatGPT alongside us? Only the brand-aware version is worth building.

positioning.sub: The one paragraph to keep in your head after closing this doc.
paragraphs: Campaign Studio is not sitting between Jasper and Skai. It is the execution platform underneath them that neither one offers: live tracking, multi-tenant from day one, encrypted credentials per customer, human approval gates, and reproducible campaigns.
Jasper sits above a platform like this and bundles a polished content interface on top. Skai sits beside it and sells media buying. The real position:
positioning.pullquote: Jasper's content intelligence on Skai's enterprise reliability, with an open connector model.
positioning.closing: Three things stand between us and saying that out loud. We need brand-from-URL, an AI search readiness score, and bulk content packs before we can stand next to Jasper. On Skai's side, the call isn't engineering. It's whether we want to play in bidding at all.
